newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. approves 120 increase in its Bosnia police unit.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves 120 increase in its Bosnia police unit.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously authorised on Friday an additional 120 police for the International Police Task Force (IPTF) in Bosnia to enable it to carry out additional human rights and training duties.
U.N. members were urged to provide qualified police monitors and other support for the force, which currently numbers about 1,700.
It was set up under the 1995 Dayton peace accords for Bosnia and works with the 31,000-strong NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR).

Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended the increase in the international police force in a March report, to enable it to investigate human rights abuses and step up the monitoring, training and restructuring of local police.

At the end of March the council approved an earlier infusion of 186 additional police and 11 civilians for the northeastern Bosnian city of Brcko, which remains under international supervision for another year.

Before the war, Moslems and Croats comprised the majority of the population of Brcko, which was captured by Bosnian Serbs in May 1992 and straddles the Posavina corridor connecting the two parts of the Serb-controlled territory of Bosnia.
